newsitem.title: GERMANY: Power plant gas use to grow sixfold by 2020.
newsitem.headline: Power plant gas use to grow sixfold by 2020.

text.p: Natural gas use in power stations worldwide is set to grow sixfold by 2020, according to the Director of Energy Technology of the European Commission's DG XVII, the energy directorate.

"Global energy consumption continues to grow, but efficiency is slow to grow with it," Pedro Miguel de Sampaio Nunes told the International Energy Agency's third natural gas conference in Berlin on Monday.
He saw gas use increasing by three percent a year for the next several years, with power generation accounting for easily the highest growth.
Nunes said that for Europe, this made security of supply from countries such as Qatar and Nigeria vital.
He also said Europe needed common energy policies, including a commitment to market liberalisation and long-term integration.
The main focus of energy technology and efficiency will be to take account of changing consumption patterns, Nunes said.

In 1990, 33 percent of the world's population used 70 percent of its energy, he said. But by 2020, according to the World Energy Council, the developing world will account for 55 percent of all energy consumption.
"In the longer term, we must think about the doubling of the world's population and climate change," Nunes said.
"These are only slowly being understood, but they need clear action. The use of energy efficiency is key, and it depends on how we use technology."
